memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Therefore, take care to follow the commands, decrees and laws I give you today. - Deut 7:11 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This short verse hinges on one important word: "therefore." Everything before it has been about God's love, God's choice, God's faithfulness, God's redemption. And because of all that, "therefore" — take care to follow His commands. The order matters immensely. Obedience is not the way we earn God's love; it is the grateful response to a love already given. God rescued them first, chose them first, loved them first — and obedience flows out of that grace.

This is the pattern of true, healthy faith. When we get the order backward — trying to obey in order to win God's approval — we end up either proud of our success or crushed by our failure. But when we grasp that God has already loved and rescued us, obedience becomes something beautiful: the natural response of a grateful heart. We do not obey to be loved; we obey because we are loved.

The whole New Testament breathes this same air. "We love because he first loved us" (1 John 4:19). Paul spends long chapters describing God's grace before he ever says "therefore" and turns to how we should live (Rom 12:1). If your obedience feels like a joyless burden or an anxious effort to earn something, return to the "therefore." Remember all that God has done for you in Christ, and let your obedience flow from gratitude, not fear. That is the only obedience that lasts and the only kind that brings joy.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do I obey God to earn His love, or as a response to love already given?
- How does the word "therefore" reshape my understanding of obedience?
- Where has my obedience become a joyless burden instead of a grateful response?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You loved me first and rescued me by grace. Let my obedience flow not from fear or striving but from a grateful heart, responding to all You have done for me in Christ. Amen.
